parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence is documented, but the exposure after discovery is serious. Worst features sit at tier 2/3: documented violence against an LGBT visitor (2017 carnival assault), unsolved murders of gay men with impunity, and a Court of Appeal endorsing force against a 'homosexual act' — gay-panic reasoning courts would likely extend to gender-nonconforming people. No hate-crime law, no gender-identity non-discrimination provision, and constitutional exclusion mean no realistic remedy; a government member publicly demanded exiling trans people. Surveys show overwhelming hostility (though measuring sexual-orientation attitudes), an underground LGBT scene, and police raids on parties. Mitigating: no criminalisation of presentation, no documented police targeting of trans people (the raid produced an apology), no documented universal facility or border rule — those remain open questions, not exposures. Dated, scattered incidents and thin trans-specific data keep this out of the 0.25 tier; unremedied hostility plus institutional impunity holds it below 0.45.
